comments.text:
​As an automotive tech, let me explain what’s actually happening here. Every modern car using an app for remote features relies on a built-in telematics module. It’s essentially a cell phone embedded in your dashboard.
​When you use the app, it sends a signal over the cellular network. Mazda pays for that SIM card's data plan for 3 years, and after that, it requires a subscription to keep the line active. This is entirely separate from traditional key fob remote start, which runs on free radio frequencies. The advertising definitely needs to be clearer, but the car isn't broken—the trial just ended.

No manufacture is currently charging you money to start your car and thats highly deceveing shame on you!
